docs.title: CI and Release Automation
docs.text:
ETLRelay uses GitHub Actions to verify changes, build and validate distributions, publish releases to PyPI, and deploy versioned documentation.

The CI workflow verifies dependency integrity, package metadata, distribution contents, installed CLI behavior, and compatibility with the supported Python versions and selected operating systems.

The production release workflow publishes a new version from main when publishing is enabled and that exact version has not already been released to PyPI.

ETLRelay retains the existing branch and publication strategy. The release-readiness checks verify the built distribution rather than relying solely on editable development installations.

docs.title: Branch strategy
docs.text:
• dev is the integration branch for active development.
  • Work-in-progress changes are developed on feature branches and merged into dev through pull requests, or committed directly to dev if working solo and that is the chosen project practice.
  • A release is promoted by opening a pull request from dev into main.
  • main is the production branch. A push to main triggers the PyPI release workflow when the release gate is enabled.
  • The release workflow publishes only when the version in pyproject.toml has not already been published to PyPI. Merging ordinary changes without a version bump therefore does not create a duplicate release.

docs.title: Release candidate preparation
docs.text:
Before opening or merging a release pull request:

  1. Set project.version in pyproject.toml to the intended release version.
  2. Regenerate uv.lock and verify it with uv lock --check.
  3. Confirm the supported Python range and default development interpreter.
  4. Update CHANGELOG.md with the actual release changes.
  5. Update the README, documentation homepage, and versioned links.
  6. Run the dependency audit and installed dependency compatibility checks.
  7. Run the full tests, coverage, lint, formatting, type-checking, and strict documentation build.
  8. Build a fresh wheel and source distribution.
  9. Validate the built artifacts using Twine and the distribution verification script.
  10. Verify clean-environment installation, CLI behavior, and a representative pipeline execution using both built artifacts.
  11. Confirm the complete CI workflow and compatibility matrix pass.
  12. Review the changeset for unintended public API changes, unsupported security claims, or out-of-scope refactoring.
  13. Complete the release checklist before promoting dev to main.

A successful editable install does not satisfy the built-artifact verification requirement.

PyPI versions cannot be overwritten. Release candidates must use an appropriate new version when a previously published artifact needs to be replaced.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: The primary CI workflow is .github/workflows/ci.yml.

docs.title: Quality job
docs.text:
The primary quality job runs on Ubuntu with Python 3.12.

It verifies:

  1. Dependency lockfile consistency using uv lock --check.
  2. Known dependency vulnerabilities and adverse package statuses using uv audit.
  3. Installed dependency compatibility using uv pip check.
  4. The full pytest suite with statement and branch coverage.
  5. Ruff linting and formatting.
  6. Pyright static analysis.
  7. Strict MkDocs documentation builds.
  8. Wheel and source-distribution construction.
  9. Distribution metadata using Twine.
  10. Distribution contents through tests/packaging/check_distributions.py.
  11. Installed CLI behavior using a wheel installed into an independent environment outside the repository checkout.

The installed CLI verification includes version/help output, configuration validation, local CSV pipeline execution, exit codes, and selected sensitive-output regression checks.

The quality job uploads the verified distribution artifacts for use by the compatibility matrix.

docs.title: Installed-artifact compatibility
docs.text:
The compatibility jobs download the same wheel and source distribution built by the quality job. The sdist is built in an isolated installation environment; the source checkout is never installed as a substitute.

Platform Python Ubuntu 3.13 Ubuntu 3.14 macOS 3.12 Windows 3.12

Each compatibility job installs each artifact into a separate clean environment, checks dependency consistency and import isolation, and exercises the installed CLI and a minimal supported CSV pipeline.

The full pytest suite runs in the primary quality job rather than being duplicated across every operating-system and Python combination.

docs.title: Verification limitations
docs.text:
The matrix does not test every possible operating-system, CPU architecture, Python-version, or database-driver combination.

A successful dependency audit identifies no currently reported vulnerabilities covered by the audit; it does not guarantee the absence of undiscovered vulnerabilities.

Distribution metadata checks confirm expected archive contents and declared metadata. Wheel and source-distribution smoke tests independently verify that representative runtime functionality works without the repository checkout.

docs.title: Coverage requirement
docs.text:
CI runs pytest with line and branch coverage and requires coverage to be strictly greater than 90% (90.1% minimum reported coverage). The build fails if the threshold is not met. The coverage configuration is in pyproject.toml.

pytest-cov must be available in a development dependency group. Ruff and Pyright must also be available in a dependency group installed by CI. If they are only supplied by the local Nix development shell, add them to a CI-only dependency group so GitHub-hosted runners can run the same checks without installing the local Nix shell.

docs.title: GitHub branch protection
docs.text:
In repository settings, protect main:

  • Require pull requests before merging.
  • Require the CI / quality status check to pass.
  • Require branches to be up to date before merging, if preferred.
  • Block force pushes and deletion.

Protect dev from accidental deletion and force pushes as appropriate. If you require pull requests into dev, also require CI / quality there. Configure the GitHub pypi environment to allow deployments from main only. Keep the production publishing job separate from the build job; only the publishing job receives id-token: write.

docs.title: CLI release verification (v0.7.0 onward)
docs.text:
Before promoting a CLI release, verify the command boundary from the built package, not only from a repository checkout:

  1. Run uv run mkdocs build --strict to catch broken navigation, missing pages, and documentation warnings.
  2. Run the functional installed-package tests that build and install the wheel in an isolated environment.
  3. Confirm etlrelay --help, etlrelay help run, and etlrelay version work from outside the repository checkout.
  4. Validate a supported local CSV configuration, run it through etlrelay run, and inspect the generated output.
  5. Verify validation does not create output and failures use the documented exit codes without printing sentinel credentials or payload values.
  6. Run the project test suite, Ruff lint/format checks, Pyright, uv build, and distribution metadata validation.

Do not mark the release ready if the strict documentation build or clean-install/installed-CLI checks remain unverified. Record any genuine environment-specific limitation explicitly and distinguish it from a product or documentation failure.

docs.title: TestPyPI procedure
docs.text:
1. Merge the release candidate into dev and make sure CI passes.
  2. In GitHub Actions, select Publish to TestPyPI, select the dev branch, and run the workflow manually.
  3. The workflow runs tests, enforces coverage, checks lint/format/types, builds the docs and distributions, then publishes the built distributions to TestPyPI.
  4. A smoke-test job creates a clean environment, installs runtime dependencies from PyPI, installs the ETLRelay package itself from TestPyPI, and checks core imports.
  5. Review the workflow result and package page on TestPyPI before promoting the same version to production.

TestPyPI versions are also immutable. If a version was already uploaded to TestPyPI, use a new pre-release version for another publishing attempt, or inspect the existing uploaded artifact instead of trying to overwrite it.

docs.title: Configure Trusted Publishing
docs.text:
Create/configure Trusted Publishers separately on TestPyPI and PyPI. These values must match the repository that actually contains the workflows:

Index Workflow file GitHub environment TestPyPI .github/workflows/publish-testpypi.yml testpypi PyPI .github/workflows/release-pypi.yml pypi

For each index, configure the repository owner and repository name exactly. Configure the workflow filename and environment name to match the table. If the project has not yet been created on that index, use that index's pending Trusted Publisher flow for the first publication.

Trusted Publishing uses GitHub's OIDC integration, so do not add a long-lived PyPI API token to GitHub secrets. The publish jobs deliberately have only id-token: write; build and test jobs do not receive it.

docs.title: Production publication behavior
docs.text:
When PYPI_RELEASE_ENABLED is exactly true, every push to main runs .github/workflows/release-pypi.yml. It reads the project name/version and checks whether that exact version exists on PyPI.

  • If it already exists, publication is skipped. This is expected for ordinary main-branch changes that do not bump the version.
  • If it is new, the workflow runs the quality gates, builds the wheel and source distribution, checks the artifacts, publishes them to PyPI, and then creates a matching vX.Y.Z GitHub release/tag.
  • If quality gates or publishing fail, no GitHub release is created.

The CI and release workflows both run checks intentionally: CI blocks unsafe merges, while the release workflow independently verifies the exact code and artifacts it publishes.

docs.title: Configuration documentation checks
docs.text:
For releases that change declarative configuration, include these documentation checks in the release review:

  • docs/configuration.md must match the implemented schema version, component registrations, validator behavior, and SQL environment preflight.
  • Runnable examples must use supported ETLRelay interfaces and remain consistent with the current release. Python configuration examples should use ConfigLoader, create_default_component_catalog(), and PipelineBuilder where appropriate. CLI examples should use the supported etlrelay validate and etlrelay run commands.
  • Release verification must include the installed CLI smoke tests, confirming that configuration validation and pipeline execution work from a built distribution outside the repository checkout.
  • README, getting-started, API reference, configuration architecture, security, changelog, roadmap, and versioned documentation links must consistently reflect the intended release.
  • Run uv run mkdocs build --strict after documentation edits to check navigation, internal links, and generated API references.
  • Run the release workflow's clean-environment smoke test against the built wheel and source distribution; do not rely only on imports from the repository checkout.

docs.title: Manual release recovery
docs.text:
If publication succeeds but GitHub release creation fails, do not change the published package version. Check whether the vX.Y.Z tag already exists and create the missing GitHub release manually for that same tag/commit. If the PyPI version exists but is wrong, publish a new version; PyPI files cannot be replaced in place.

The shared compatibility smoke script now defaults to testing both artifacts in separate environments. TestPyPI and PyPI verification workflows use this same script before publication. See the packaging verification record for commands and evidence.

docs.title: v1.0.0 stable release promotion
docs.text:
The package version is 1.0.0. The changelog and release notes use the target date 2026-10-21; update both if publication moves. The compatibility policy applies to the stable public contract. No Python or YAML migration is required from v0.9.0.

Use the existing TestPyPI procedure on dev, then promote the reviewed source to main. The production workflow creates v1.0.0 after publication and uses docs/development/release-notes-v1.0.0.md for the GitHub release body. Versioned documentation deploys under 1.0.0; repository content links use v1.0.0. Do not create the release tag before the workflow or overwrite published files.

Complete RELEASE_CHECKS.md against the integrated release commit. The readiness record distinguishes prior v0.9.0 support evidence, local v1.0.0 checks, required final CI, and publication. External beta feedback and an RC cycle are optional; readiness is established through maintainer verification. No deployment is implied by a successful local build.

docs.title: ETLRelay v0.9.0 — Release Notes
docs.text:
Release date: 2026-10-21.

ETLRelay v0.9.0 freezes the intended v1.0 feature set and reviews its public API, component interactions, failure behavior, documentation, and package installation. The supported product remains synchronous pipelines using local CSV/Parquet or SQL, the existing processors, YAML configuration, and the CLI.

docs.title: Public API Review
docs.text:
• Rename Reader and Writer to TabularReader and TabularWriter to identify their batch-oriented contracts. The old class names are removed without aliases; the existing modules and concrete format-class names remain unchanged.
  • Keep KeyValueReader separate for mapping-shaped documents. Mapping-document writing and generic tabular/row-record conversion remain deferred.
  • Retain YAML configuration schema version 1 and the current CLI command set.

docs.title: Correctness and Failure Handling
docs.text:
• Report invalid YAML document shapes as CLI configuration failures with exit code 3, using YamlDocumentError, a compatible ValueError subclass.
  • Reject ambiguous column selection with ValueError and enforce unique final names when renaming columns, including duplicate input fields.
  • Preserve the original error if Parquet finalization also fails. Report secondary cleanup failures without exposing their exception messages.

docs.title: Testing and Distribution Verification
docs.text:
• Record representative Python, YAML, and installed-CLI coverage across local CSV, Parquet, and SQLite source/sink boundaries.
  • Extend failure coverage for borrowed streams, partial outputs, SQL connection and conversion failures, transaction behavior, and controlled diagnostics.
  • Install wheels and source distributions separately outside the checkout.
  • Check complete runtime dependency requirements, source modules, licence/notice files, and console entry points.
  • Remove the unused Polars runtime dependency; retain PyArrow-based processing.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Provide a self-contained CLI/Python quick start and verify shipped examples against a built, installed candidate.
  • Document extension through Python protocols, schema/validation boundaries, troubleshooting, security limits, and migration requirements.
  • Record the exact support matrix and the frozen v1.0 boundary.

docs.title: Dependencies and Tooling
docs.text: • Refresh dependency and release tooling, including SQLAlchemy, Ruff, mkdocstrings, and GitHub Actions dependencies.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
Update imports and annotations from Reader/Writer to TabularReader/TabularWriter. Review catches for ambiguous column selection and CLI automation that previously treated invalid YAML document shapes as internal failures. Applications using Polars must declare their own dependency.

See Migration to v0.9.0 for import mappings and behavior changes. No YAML schema migration is required.

docs.title: Support and Limitations
docs.text:
CPython 3.12–3.14 is supported in the five declared Python/platform combinations; full tests run on Ubuntu/3.12, with installed-artifact smoke checks on the remaining matrix entries. SQLite is the reference database; other SQLAlchemy dialects need appropriate drivers and independent verification.

Local writes truncate existing files and are not atomic. SQL sinks append to existing tables using per-batch transactions. SQL source results are materialized in memory. Safe diagnostics do not sanitize arbitrary third-party exceptions or application logging. Path containment is not a filesystem sandbox.

S3/HDFS, additional formats/processors, dynamic plugins, scheduling, automatic retries, distributed execution, schema reconciliation, SQL table creation/upsert, KeyValueWriter, and generic record conversion remain outside the v1.0 boundary.

The scope policy, API review, pipeline coverage, failure matrix, and packaging verification provide supporting detail. See Beta readiness and feedback for the review decision, verification evidence, remaining publication gates, and reporting criteria.

docs.title: ETLRelay v1.0.0 — Stable Initial Release
docs.text:
Release date: 2026-10-21.

ETLRelay v1.0.0 establishes the stable public contract for the feature set completed and verified in v0.9.0. It supports synchronous pipelines using local CSV/Parquet or SQL input/output, the existing processors, direct Python composition, YAML configuration, and the CLI.

docs.title: Stable Public Contract
docs.text:
• Publish the compatibility and versioning policy for documented Python imports, constructors/protocols, data and failure semantics, YAML schema version 1, CLI behavior, and supported environments.
  • Define patch/minor/major release rules and public deprecation/migration policy.
  • Retain TabularReader/TabularWriter and the separate mapping-document KeyValueReader contract introduced before the API freeze.

docs.title: Release and Documentation Readiness
docs.text:
• Update package metadata, installation commands, CLI version examples, security policy, release documentation, and version-pinned content links for v1.0.0.
  • Complete the v0.9.0 publication record and retain its review evidence.
  • Verify release artifacts and supported environments using the existing checks.
  • Establish maintainer verification as the acceptance mechanism; external beta feedback and release candidates are optional.

docs.title: Post-v1.0 Direction
docs.text:
• Replace detailed pre-1.0 milestone checklists with a concise release history and a selected post-v1.0 plan.
  • Expand the selected plan through targeted 1.1–1.14 milestones: SQL batching, PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB/SQL Server/Oracle, common transformations, S3/Azure/GCS, Excel/JSON/Arrow interchange, trusted extensions, directory/regex consolidation, partitioned datasets, append/upsert/overwrite modes, APIs, watermark loads, DuckDB, and cloud warehouses.
  • Target Python 3.15 through a separately verified dependency/compatibility upgrade. Require separate dependency and account-backed verification for Snowflake/BigQuery. Keep document pipelines, specialist integrations, continuous streaming and distributed execution subject to explicit review.
  • Separate tentative future features from the selected milestones, with explicit feasibility/need conditions. Retain all new work outside v1.0.0 support until implemented and released.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Applications using v0.9.0 require no Python or YAML migration. The runtime source, constructor/protocol signatures, processors, schema version, CLI commands and exit codes, dependency bounds, cleanup behavior, and persistence semantics are unchanged. Install the stable release with:

python -m pip install etlrelay==1.0.0

For releases before v0.9.0, follow the v0.9.0 migration guide, including the tabular protocol rename. The former Reader/Writer class names have no compatibility aliases.

docs.title: Support and Known Limitations
docs.text:
CPython 3.12–3.14 is supported in the five declared combinations: Ubuntu with 3.12/3.13/3.14, macOS with 3.12, and Windows with 3.12. The full suite runs on Ubuntu/3.12; both-artifact smoke checks cover the other entries. SQLite is the tested database. Other SQLAlchemy dialects need drivers and independent verification and are not guaranteed support.

Local output writes are non-atomic and may truncate or leave partial/unreadable files. SQL sinks append to existing compatible tables with per-batch transactions; earlier commits survive later failures. SQL source results are materialized in memory. Path containment is not a sandbox; ETLRelay-controlled diagnostics do not sanitize arbitrary third-party exceptions or application logs.

S3/HDFS, additional formats/processors/integrations, mapping-document writing, generic record conversion, dynamic plugins, SQL creation/upsert or pipeline-wide transactions, scheduling, retries, and concurrent/distributed execution remain outside this release's scope. Future capabilities will be evaluated through a separate post-v1.0 roadmap.

See the scope policy, API reference, security guidance, and readiness record for contracts, evidence, and release gates. Report reproducible defects with synthetic data through GitHub Issues; report suspected vulnerabilities privately through the Security Policy.

docs.title: Release decision and scope
docs.text:
The v1.0.0 source is prepared from the officially released v0.9.0 feature set. No required runtime feature remains incomplete and no open product defect was found in the public issue review. The only open issue at review was #142; prerequisite #139 and parent milestone #37 are closed. Repeat the issue check before promotion.

This release changes metadata, policy, release records, and documentation. Runtime source, tests, workflow definitions, runtime dependency bounds, and the resolved third-party dependency versions are unchanged from the baseline. There is no additional API change or YAML migration from v0.9.0.

The stable compatibility policy covers the documented Python imports and signatures, tabular/schema semantics, YAML schema version 1, CLI contracts, exceptions, ownership, and persistence behavior. Compatible fixes use patch releases, compatible additions use minor releases, and breaking public changes require a major release. Deprecations retain compatibility during 1.x.

External beta participation and a release-candidate cycle are optional. Maintainer verification is the acceptance mechanism. This record does not claim external feedback, v1.0.0 publication, or final CI has occurred.

docs.text:
Follow the existing release procedure and complete the active RELEASE_CHECKS.md:

docs.title: Limitations and later work
docs.text:
The scope policy and security guidance retain non-atomic/partial file output, append-only per-batch SQL commits, materialized SQL reads, explicit resource ownership, filesystem race/security limitations, and the boundary of controlled diagnostic redaction. These are supported, documented operational constraints and are not unimplemented release features.

Remote storage, more formats/processors/integrations, conversion frameworks, scheduling/retries, concurrency/distribution, dynamic plugins, and additional SQL modes remain deferred. The post-v1.0 roadmap will separately evaluate concrete user workflows, adoption benefits, architectural fit, and maintenance cost, including whether an idea belongs in the core, an optional integration, a companion project, or an existing external tool. No such feature is required for this release.

docs.title: v1.0 Feature Scope and Support Policy
docs.text:
This document defines ETLRelay v1.0.0 support and the feature boundary verified during v0.9.0.

The v1.0.0 release retains the reviewed v0.9.0 runtime feature set. See the compatibility policy for the stable contract and the v1.0.0 readiness record for final verification/publication gates. External beta feedback is optional and does not block release.

docs.title: Feature Freeze
docs.text:
The v1.0 feature set is frozen.

Changes during v1.0.0 release preparation must address:

  • Correctness.
  • Security.
  • Compatibility within the declared support matrix.
  • Public API clarity and consistency.
  • Testing, documentation, packaging, or release readiness.

New formats, storage backends, processors, integrations, and execution models are deferred.

Any exception must identify a concrete requirement that prevents the agreed v1.0 feature set from working correctly. Record its justification, acceptance criteria, and affected ticket before implementation.

docs.title: Python and Platform Support
docs.text:
The supported interpreter family is CPython 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.

Package metadata declares:

requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"

Python 3.12 is the default development interpreter and the configured static-analysis target.

The release support matrix is the following set of combinations, rather than every combination of the listed Python versions and operating systems:

Platform CPython Required verification Ubuntu 3.12 Full test suite, coverage, quality checks, documentation build, distribution checks, and installed wheel/sdist verification Ubuntu 3.13 Installed wheel/sdist compatibility smoke tests Ubuntu 3.14 Installed wheel/sdist compatibility smoke tests macOS 3.12 Installed wheel/sdist compatibility smoke tests Windows 3.12 Installed wheel/sdist compatibility smoke tests

The compatibility smoke test installs the wheel and source distribution separately and verifies isolated installation, public imports, dependency consistency, direct CSV/Parquet/SQLite composition, CLI help/version, YAML validation, and a minimal CSV CLI pipeline.

Smoke coverage does not imply that the full test suite runs on every matrix entry.

CI uses GitHub-hosted *-latest runners. This policy does not promise particular operating-system releases or CPU architectures beyond those actually exercised by the release checks.

Other Python/platform combinations may work but are not release-supported or independently verified. Other Python implementations and Python versions outside the declared range are not supported.

The matrix records required checks. Successful release verification must be established from actual CI results.

docs.title: Storage, Format, and Database Support
docs.text:
Area v1.0 support File storage LocalFileSystem Tabular file input/output CSV and Parquet Configuration documents Mapping-shaped YAML using schema version 1 SQL reference backend SQLite through SQLAlchemy Other SQLAlchemy dialects Unverified compatibility; not guaranteed support

Other SQLAlchemy dialects require appropriate drivers and independent verification of queries, identifiers, type conversion, reflection, transactions, and cleanup. SQLAlchemy compatibility alone does not establish ETLRelay support for a database.

SQLite is the required database backend for repeatable automated integration and functional tests. External database services are not required for v1.0 release verification.

docs.title: Operational Boundaries
docs.text:
• Execution is synchronous and batch-oriented.
  • Processors run in their configured order.
  • Output schema compatibility is enforced during execution.
  • Entirely empty sources do not invoke the sink.
  • Zero-row batches still participate in processing and schema validation.
  • File sources/sinks own streams they open; readers/writers borrow supplied streams.
  • Pipeline execution attempts to close active iterators exposing callable close() methods.
  • Local output writes are not atomic and may truncate existing files or leave partial output.
  • SQL sinks append using one transaction per nonempty batch; earlier commits survive later failures.
  • Direct Python SQL callers own their engines. Configuration-built engines follow the builder's documented lifecycle.
  • Path containment is not a complete filesystem sandbox.
  • ETLRelay-controlled diagnostics have documented protections; arbitrary third-party exceptions and application logging are not guaranteed to be sanitized.

Mapping-shaped documents are distinct from sequences of row records. KeyValueReader remains separate from the tabular reader/writer protocols.
